- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤-1.0) mid-period, model often underreacts; adjust upward to reflect sentiment shift.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in next period; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >+3% across 3–5 days), consider mean reversion bias — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– signals, model often misreads momentum; align forecast with sentiment direction, not just price trend.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate late-period price peaks (last 5–7 days); add 0.5–1.5% buffer to final 5–7 forecast points if sentiment is bullish.
- If model forecast is below true outcome by >2% for 3+ consecutive days, consider lagged sentiment effect — forecast may be catching up; adjust upward by 0.3–0.7% per day.
